criteria.criterion: a configured `provider` is honoured for a model id containing a colon: a class configured `{model: "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", provider: "bedrock"}` resolves to `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`
an ALREADY-qualified string is still not double-prefixed: `bedrock:us.anthropic.…-v1:0` stays unchanged

the qualified/unqualified decision is NO LONGER made by the presence of a colon, and both deciders (`_resolve_target` and `infer_provider`) route through ONE shared function (`split_provider_qualifier`)
GUARD ORDER: an explicitly configured `provider` is checked FIRST, before the model string is scanned at all
a conflicting configured-provider / inline-qualifier pair RAISES rather than silently picking a winner
a bare id with no configured provider still infers as it does today (back-compat: every existing unversioned value resolves byte-for-byte unchanged)
tests cover BOTH Bedrock id shapes — unversioned alias and canonical `...-v1:0` — because the unversioned form passes even against the bug and is what hid it
`infer_provider` agrees with the qualifier on every shape the tests cover
the reported failure mode is gone: no diagnostic reports a fragment of a model id as though it were a configured provider
[Delegated to 7b22] the qualified/unqualified decision is made against the REGISTERED PROVIDER SET rather than by prefix shape
[Delegated to 7b22] a provider name that is not registered produces a diagnostic naming the invalid provider and listing the valid ones
[Delegated to 7b22] back-compat is enumerated and tested against the runtime registries
